name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
description: Adversaries abuse command and script interpreters (bash, PowerShell, cmd, Python) to execute commands, scripts, or binaries.

name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
description: Adversaries exploit a weakness in an Internet-facing host or application to gain initial access to a network.

name: Valid Accounts
description: Adversaries obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts to gain access, persist, escalate, or evade defenses.

name: Brute Force
description: Adversaries guess passwords or keys through systematic trial, including password guessing, spraying, and credential stuffing.

name: Network Service Discovery
description: Adversaries enumerate services running on remote hosts and network infrastructure, often via port and vulnerability scans.

name: Application Layer Protocol
description: Adversaries communicate with controlled systems using OSI application-layer protocols such as HTTP, DNS, or mail to blend with normal traffic.

name: Remote Services
description: Adversaries use valid accounts to log into remote services like SSH, RDP, SMB, or VNC and move laterally.

name: Process Injection
description: Adversaries inject code into live processes to evade process-based defenses and possibly elevate privileges.

name: OS Credential Dumping
description: Adversaries dump credential material such as account hashes from the OS, memory (LSASS), or the SAM/NTDS databases.

name: Scheduled Task/Job
description: Adversaries abuse task scheduling (cron, at, schtasks, systemd timers) to run malicious code on a schedule or at startup.

name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
description: Adversaries bypass elevation controls such as sudo, setuid/setgid, or UAC to execute code with higher privileges.

name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
description: Adversaries exploit software vulnerabilities, often kernel or driver flaws, to execute code with elevated privileges.

name: External Remote Services
description: Adversaries leverage external-facing remote services such as VPNs, Citrix, or RDP gateways to access a network.

name: Phishing
description: Adversaries send phishing messages with malicious attachments or links to gain access to victim systems.

name: Ingress Tool Transfer
description: Adversaries transfer tools or other files from an external system into a compromised environment.

name: System Information Discovery
description: Adversaries gather detailed information about the operating system and hardware, including version, patches, and architecture.

name: Process Discovery
description: Adversaries enumerate running processes to understand software and security tooling present on a host.

name: File and Directory Discovery
description: Adversaries enumerate files and directories or search specific locations for information of interest.

name: Software Discovery
description: Adversaries enumerate installed software and versions, including security software, to shape follow-on actions.

name: Create Account
description: Adversaries create local, domain, or cloud accounts to maintain persistent access to a system or network.
